Minimum Unrestricted Cash at October 31, 2026 fails. The bank calculated {{fact:6146fce8-6828-45e8-8d09-520a933d9a5f}} against a minimum of {{fact:f6d827f0-e9d2-44ca-bb69-b9e1138d06ca}}, a headroom of {{fact:c805c23f-be8c-4aa8-88e2-6cd4a3745a93}}. The borrower certified {{fact:2917bbbd-a5ea-4095-8725-da43f739f2ea}} and reported compliance. The certificate's schedule reaches that figure by adding the balance of the pledged collateral account to cash in the operating accounts. Section 1.1 of the agreement excludes pledged or restricted cash from Unrestricted Cash. The October account statement marks the collateral account as restricted and pledged to secure a letter of credit. When that account is left out, operating-account cash matches the bank's figure. Only the approved version of the terms is on file, and no amendment or waiver is on file. The Series B term sheet is dated after the test date, is non-binding and does not change the covenant. I reran the test under the approved terms and it still fails. The breach appears to be real, and it comes from the borrower's calculation.

Minimum Unrestricted Cash at October 31, 2026 fails. The bank calculated {{fact:6146fce8-6828-45e8-8d09-520a933d9a5f}} against a minimum of {{fact:f6d827f0-e9d2-44ca-bb69-b9e1138d06ca}} (headroom {{fact:c805c23f-be8c-4aa8-88e2-6cd4a3745a93}}). The borrower certified {{fact:2917bbbd-a5ea-4095-8725-da43f739f2ea}} and compliance. Its schedule adds the pledged collateral account to operating-account cash. Section 1.1 excludes pledged or restricted cash from Unrestricted Cash, and the October bank statement marks that account as restricted and pledged for a letter of credit. Without it, operating-account cash matches the bank's figure. Only the approved terms version is on file, and no amendment or waiver is on file. The Series B term sheet postdates the test date and is non-binding. Rerun under the approved terms, the test still fails. The breach appears real and stems from the borrower's calculation.

At current burn, Datamarrow's cash covers about {{fact:8f300210-8c4b-43bf-9cc0-804bcd2748fa}} months of operations, short enough that its ability to keep paying depends on new funding or cost cuts arriving soon. The falling runway covenant headroom and the cash covenant now below its minimum point the same way.

Negative headroom means unrestricted cash of {{fact:8a2dd349-b6e5-41ab-b6be-05954633108a}} is below the covenant minimum of {{fact:f02ef0d7-f49b-4879-8c50-3da80f1f8d73}}, so on these figures the covenant appears breached at October 31, not merely tight. Together with the short runway, this shows the cash cushion has run out ahead of the borrower's funding needs.

Cash covenant headroom slid from {{fact:58788de3-1f23-4c5a-b9b3-f70319889371}} in August to {{fact:f7b3092c-8a02-4a1e-8166-76961836cda5}} in September and {{fact:3715b198-c83d-4976-a358-475f45a8c0f3}} in October. The steady decline shows the breach is the result of continued burn rather than a one-off dip, which makes a quick recovery less likely without new cash.

Runway covenant headroom fell from {{fact:9119883a-3477-4266-90d4-501683a7d484}} in August to {{fact:59550f11-9b7d-499d-96dd-e704fa1f8ab2}} in September and {{fact:29b15a39-9b32-4a02-addb-4aa9e5516240}} in October, with runway of {{fact:0b76f42f-c135-46ee-833e-5b635a156b4d}} months against a minimum of {{fact:4f5a1d78-edc8-4b67-8e12-c2cea7c2e95a}}. The covenant still passes, but if the pace continues it could follow the cash covenant below its minimum.

The Total Leverage Ratio for the period ended September 30, 2026 tests at {{fact:6c64c6af-9d31-495c-834b-a3e4598b8214}} against a maximum of {{fact:3489f876-708a-41af-8dd3-d7e2bba7a6cf}}, while the certificate reports {{fact:c024d5d7-8ac5-488d-a112-ad6dd7239fc0}} and compliance. In Schedule 1 of the certificate, the borrower's Total Debt and EBITDA components match the bank's inputs. The gap comes from one line the borrower added to EBITDA: pro forma cost savings from plant consolidation. The Credit Agreement's EBITDA definition (Section 1.1) allows only interest expense, income tax expense, and depreciation and amortization to be added back. It has no provision for pro forma cost savings. No amendments or other terms versions are on file. Rerunning the test under the approved terms (version 1) confirms the failure. The breach appears real, and the certificate's compliance statement rests on an add-back the agreement does not permit.

Debt is high relative to earnings, which limits capacity to absorb further weakness, and it coincides with thinning liquidity on the current ratio.

The current ratio of {{fact:5827c54c-d223-4433-9da6-f42e19574a9b}} is only slightly above the {{fact:0ff32e60-18ef-4f79-b8d1-6cce73cb9aef}} minimum, leaving headroom of {{fact:f46dc689-fdec-4d08-9134-e8c793275314}}. Short-term liquidity is tightening at the same time leverage is over its limit, so both the balance sheet and near-term cash cover are under pressure.

Revenue to Plan (Section 6.3) fails for the three months ended October 31, 2026. Revenue was {{fact:5cedbc4e-c921-4d52-9089-0b6173a9d3b7}} of the Approved Plan, below the required minimum of {{fact:fab6c434-829a-414b-9b21-82efccc7f846}}. The borrower's October certificate reports the same figure, {{fact:7043f3c1-fb85-4781-a705-abe866afa2d8}}, and states it was not in compliance. Approved terms version 1 is the only version on file, and no amendments are waiting for approval. Searches of the documents found no waiver and no written update to the Approved Plan. I reran the test under version 1 and it still fails: {{fact:1590dcf0-b844-4a84-94b8-44307dc20e6a}} against {{fact:cae095c8-3e12-45fa-a67c-a4bd3618b79f}}, a shortfall of {{fact:3d5a1fbc-46b3-4348-86d4-c5a3a193c593}} relative to the requirement. The September certificate also reported non-compliance with this covenant, so the shortfall goes back more than one period. Nothing found explains the failure, so it appears to be a real breach.

Revenue to Plan (Section 6.3) fails for the three months ended October 31, 2026. Revenue was {{fact:5cedbc4e-c921-4d52-9089-0b6173a9d3b7}} of the Approved Plan, below the required minimum of {{fact:fab6c434-829a-414b-9b21-82efccc7f846}}. The borrower's October certificate reports the same figure, {{fact:7043f3c1-fb85-4781-a705-abe866afa2d8}}, and states it was not in compliance. The approved terms in force are the only version on file, and no amendments are waiting for approval. Searches of the documents found no waiver and no written update to the Approved Plan. I reran the test under the approved terms and it still fails: {{fact:1590dcf0-b844-4a84-94b8-44307dc20e6a}} against {{fact:cae095c8-3e12-45fa-a67c-a4bd3618b79f}}, a shortfall of {{fact:3d5a1fbc-46b3-4348-86d4-c5a3a193c593}} relative to the requirement. The September certificate also reported non-compliance with this covenant, so the shortfall did not begin in October. Nothing found explains the failure, so it appears to be a real breach.

Revenue reached {{fact:5cedbc4e-c921-4d52-9089-0b6173a9d3b7}} of plan against a covenant floor of {{fact:fab6c434-829a-414b-9b21-82efccc7f846}}. That leaves headroom of {{fact:c6096120-13ce-475a-9a3c-4e094325bc77}}, so the covenant level is not being met rather than merely close. The revenue-below-plan and falling-headroom signals describe the same shortfall.

Revenue came in at {{fact:4a4f0bb9-3a15-4347-8b3a-418c7d837422}} of plan. For a SaaS borrower, that points to weaker bookings, churn or delayed renewals. This is the operating cause behind the revenue covenant shortfall, and it may also explain the steady erosion in cash headroom.

Revenue covenant headroom has slid each month: from {{fact:a3d32892-415e-4ce2-a815-1e48301ef46b}} in August, to {{fact:9d7c8bcf-02d3-4c27-be80-968f759493fb}} in September, to {{fact:c6096120-13ce-475a-9a3c-4e094325bc77}} in October. The shortfall began in September and deepened in October, so it is a worsening trend rather than a one-month miss.

Unrestricted cash of {{fact:05898ae8-c3b4-4ddc-8d29-7e1f05777a3a}} remains comfortably above the {{fact:c2862161-e6bf-4c1d-8148-0fd47e025235}} minimum. However, headroom has declined steadily, from {{fact:00990abf-473d-4ab5-b4ca-1208c0ed0a27}} to {{fact:3d5c18ef-2671-4f3b-beab-7a8b3d8f5831}} to {{fact:58b78aa2-6632-4582-a3c7-c4fe8e4f7576}}. Taken together with the revenue shortfall, this suggests cash burn is drawing down the liquidity cushion.
